questions.stem: When solving the equation \(\dfrac{21+4x}{3} = 18\), which step should be performed last?

steps.explain: To undo the operations in the correct order, work from the outside in: first undo the division by 3, then the addition of 21, then the multiplication by 4.
Next undo the "+21" by subtracting 21 from both sides.
The last step left to undo the "\(\times 4\)" is to divide both sides by 4. Pitfall: doing "÷4" too early (before removing the ÷3 and +21) breaks the order of operations and gives a wrong value of x.

questions.stem: A rectangle (not to scale) has one side labelled 10 and the OPPOSITE side labelled \(4-2x\). Since opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, write an equation and find the value of \(x\).
questions.hint: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal in length, so set the two expressions equal to each other: \(4-2x=10\).

steps.explain: Since it is a rectangle, opposite sides are equal in length. Set the two expressions for the pair of opposite sides equal to each other.
Subtract 4 from both sides to isolate the \(x\) term.

Divide both sides by \(-2\). Pitfall: dividing 6 by \(-2\) but forgetting to keep the negative sign (giving \(x=3\), option A, instead of \(x=-3\)) — a negative divided by a negative only gives a positive when BOTH numbers are negative; here only the divisor is.
Other pitfalls: moving the "4" to the wrong side (adding instead of subtracting) gives \(-2x=14 \implies x=-7\) (option D); flipping which side is subtracted from which gives \(x=7\) (option B).

questions.stem: The solution to the equation \(5 - 2(x-3) = 6\) is:

steps.explain: Expand the bracket first, being careful with the negative sign in front of it.
Simplify the left side, then isolate the \(x\)-term.
Divide both sides by \(-2\). Pitfall: expanding \(-2(x-3)\) as \(-2x - 6\) instead of \(-2x + 6\) (sign error on the second term) leads to \(x = -\dfrac{7}{2}\) instead of the correct answer.

topics.title: Equations with pronumerals on both sides

questions.hint: Expand the bracket, collect the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other.

steps.explain: Expand the bracket on the left side.
Add \(2x\) to both sides to collect all the \(x\) terms on the left, then subtract 36 from both sides to isolate the \(x\) term.
Divide both sides by 5. Pitfall: forgetting to move BOTH the \(x\) term and the constant (e.g. only moving one of them) leaves an equation that still has terms on both sides.

Other pitfalls: expanding the bracket incorrectly as \(3x+12\) (only multiplying the first term, forgetting \(3\times12=36\)) leads to \(x=-1\dfrac{2}{5}\) (option A); stopping after \(5x=-31\) without dividing gives \(x=-31\) (option B); a sign slip moving 36 across (adding instead of subtracting) gives \(x=8\dfrac{1}{5}\) (option D).

steps.explain: Collect the \(x\) terms on one side by subtracting \(7x\) from both sides, and the constants on the other by adding 2 to both sides.
Simplify both sides.

Divide both sides by \(-3\). Pitfall: a sign slip when moving the "-2" (subtracting 2 instead of adding) gives \(-3x=7 \implies x=-\dfrac{7}{3}\) (option C); adding the \(x\) terms instead of subtracting gives \(11x=11 \implies x=1\) (option D).

questions.stem: Alison is \(a\) years old and Brendan is \(b\) years old. In 10 years' time their combined age will be 40. An equation that represents this scenario is:

steps.explain: In 10 years, Alison will be \(a+10\) years old and Brendan will be \(b+10\) years old.
Their combined age in 10 years is the sum of these two expressions, which equals 40.
Simplify by collecting the constant terms. Pitfall: adding only one lot of 10 (giving \(a+b+10=40\)) forgets that BOTH people age 10 years, not just their combined total.
